title: Police deny coverup
article: For the second time in less than two months, Vancouver police are investigating the death of a man who died in custody following the use of a Taser gun.
In the latest case, police kept the incident secret for a full month before disclosing it Friday at a press conference where they vehemently defended the use of the devices.
On June 23, a Taser that delivers a 50,000-volt shock was used on 54-year-old Robert Wayne Bagnell, who police say was strung out on cocaine at a downtown rooming house.

Bagnell is at least the fourth person to die in B.C. in little over a year after being subjected to a Taser strike. Two men, one in Burnaby and one in Prince George, died last summer after being hit with Tasers.
Police spokeswoman Const. Sarah Bloor said Bagnell was destroying a washroom and was in a frenzied state.
In an effort to subdue him, an officer from the city's Emergency Response Team fired the Taser and, shortly after, Bagnell stopped breathing. He died at the scene.
She said a toxicology report on Bagnell showed he had "lethal levels" of cocaine, as well as other drugs, in his bloodstream.
The case is still under investigation by the Major Crimes division.
The officer involved in the incident remains on the job and has not been suspended, Bloor said.

Vancouver Chief Const. Jamie Graham denied his department was trying to cover up the death, especially in light of the fact it occurred less than two months after the May 1 death of Roman Andreichik in another downtown apartment. Andreichik also died after being hit with a Taser. His death is also under investigation.

Graham said he wanted to wait until toxicology reports on Bagnell were completed to show that his death was not attributable to the Taser, and that it may have been caused by the man's extreme use of drugs.
"I give you my word we waited for the toxicology so we could give a fair and balanced account of this incident," he said.

Bagnell's death came at an extremely sensitive time for the police department. A coroner's inquest into the in-custody death of Jeff Berg began the day Bagnell also died in custody. On the same day, Graham held a press conference defending the use of force by two city police officers accused of beating two men during the Guns 'N' Roses riot.
Coroner Stephen Fonseca said the cause of Bagnell's death hasn't yet been determined, but there will be a full inquest since technically he died in police custody.
"There is no definitive cause of death yet," Fonseca said. "The pathologist has not yet determined the cause."
The gun, which looks like a stumpy version of a semi-automatic pistol, uses two electrodes to cause temporary paralysis.
The shock causes severe muscle contractions between the two electrode points and disrupts the central nervous system, usually making it impossible for the victim to perform co-ordinated actions.
Often, the strike leaves the victim curled in a semi-fetal position.
The Taser uses compressed nitrogen gas to fire the electrodes up to seven metres. They are connected to the gun by two thin wires. But the gun can also be used in direct contact with the target.
Police and the gun's manufacturer, Arizona-based Taser International, say the gun temporarily incapacitates a person, and that there are no lasting effects.
But the increasing use of the Taser as a means to subdue unco- operative people has raised concerns about whether it is also causing unnecessary death.

At least 44 people have died across North America from complications following the use of the gun, and in the U.S. medical examiners cite Tasers as a cause or contributing factor in the in- custody deaths of three people.

Taser International denies the gun is responsible for any deaths, citing other factors such as drug use and heart conditions of victims. It says the gun has been shown overwhelmingly to save lives where the only other alternative would have been lethal force.

The Canada Safety Council has also begun raising concerns. Earlier this month it suggested the federal government investigate after a former semi-pro boxer died in Ontario after he was hit with the gun.
